question: Should ClawHub intentionally reject recognized case-colliding package files across all new publishes, updates, scans, and GitHub imports, even when an affected package previously worked on a case-sensitive filesystem?
rationale: The patch consistently fixes a demonstrated portability failure, but it deliberately invalidates an existing package shape and the linked issue is still marked as needing a product decision.

options.title: Enforce uniform rejection
options.body: Accept the compatibility change and land the consistent fail-closed validation with its existing rename guidance and coverage.

options.title: Require transition handling
options.body: Pause merge until affected-package prevalence is measured and maintainers define warning, migration, or grandfathering behavior.

recommendation.title: Enforce uniform rejection
recommendation.body: Accept the compatibility change and land the consistent fail-closed validation with its existing rename guidance and coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal connects this person to the central server-side skill publishing path where the compatibility policy is ultimately enforced.
